---
title: "Markdown"
subtitle: "Cheat sheet for the Markdown extra (used in READMEs, Quarto and notebooks)"
---

## Text

| You write | You get |
|------------|------------------------|
| `# Title`, `## Section`, `### Subsection` | headings (one `#` per document, sections from `##`) |
| a blank line | a new paragraph (a single line break is ignored) |
| `*italic*`, `**bold**`, `~~struck~~` | *italic*, **bold**, ~~struck~~ |
| `` `code` `` | `code` |
| `[text](https://quarto.org)` | a link: [text](https://quarto.org) |
| `<https://quarto.org>` | a bare link: <https://quarto.org> |
| `![Alt text](results/figure.png)` | an image; the alt text says what it shows |
| `> A quotation.` | a block quote |

## Lists and code

````{.markdown}
- a bullet
- another bullet
  - two spaces in: a sub-bullet

1. numbered
2. list

```bash
pixi run reproduce
```
````

Leave a blank line before lists, code blocks, tables and headings. Give code
blocks a language (`bash`, `python`, `yaml`).

## Tables

```{.markdown}
| Sample     | Generation | Variants |
|------------|-----------:|---------:|
| SRR2589044 |      5,000 |       10 |
| SRR2584866 |     50,000 |      775 |
```

In the second line, `---:` aligns right and `:---:` centres. Tables made from
data belong in code ([Quarto](quarto.qmd)), not typed.

## What Quarto adds

```{.markdown}
::: {.callout-note}
A box that draws attention. Also callout-tip, -warning, -important.
:::

See @fig-quality and @tbl-reads.      (cross-references to labelled cells)
As shown by @tenaillon2016.           (a citation from references.bib)
```

See [the Markdown extra](../pages/A-markdown.qmd#what-quarto-adds) and the [Quarto cheat sheet](quarto.qmd).

## Official cheat sheets and references

- **CommonMark quick reference**, from the CommonMark project that standardizes Markdown (with a 10-minute tutorial): <https://commonmark.org/help/>
- Quarto, *Markdown Basics*: <https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html>
- GitHub Docs, *Basic writing and formatting syntax* (Markdown in READMEs, issues and pull requests): <https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax>
